title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, The Means of Grace. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.
You have gone away from my ordinances, and have not kept them. Malachi 3:7.

title: Are there any ordinances now
english: But are there any ordinances now, since life and immortality were brought to light by the gospel? Are there, under the Christian dispensation, any means ordained by God as the usual channels of his grace? This question could never have been proposed in the apostolic church, unless by one who openly avowed himself to be a Heathen. The whole body of Christians was agreed that Christ had ordained certain outward means for conveying his grace into the souls of men.

Their constant practice set this beyond all dispute. For so long as all who believed were together, and had all things in common, Acts 2:44, they continued steadfastly in the teaching of the apostles, and in the breaking of bread, and in prayers, Acts 2:42.

title: Mistaking the means for the end
english: But in process of time, when the love of many grew cold (Matthew 24:12), some began to mistake the means for the end, and to place religion rather in doing those outward works than in a heart renewed after the image of God.

They forgot that the end of every commandment is love, out of a pure heart, with unfeigned faith (1 Timothy 1:5): loving the Lord their God with all their heart, and their neighbor as themselves (Mark 12:30-31), and being purified from pride, anger, and evil desire, by a faith of the operation of God (Colossians 2:12).

Others seemed to imagine that, though religion did not principally consist in these outward means, yet there was something in them with which God was well pleased, something that would still make them acceptable in his sight, though they were not exact in the weightier matters of the law, in justice, mercy, and the love of God.

It is evident that, in those who abused them in this way, the means did not lead to the end for which they were ordained. Rather, the things which should have been for their health were to them an occasion of falling. They were so far from receiving any blessing in them that they only drew down a curse upon their head. They were so far from growing more heavenly in heart and life that they were twofold more the children of hell than before.

Others, clearly perceiving that these means did not convey the grace of God to those children of the devil, began from this particular case to draw a general conclusion, that they were not means of conveying the grace of God.

title: Men who knew inward religion
english: Yet the number of those who abused the ordinances of God was far greater than the number of those who despised them, until certain men arose. They were men not only of great understanding, sometimes joined with considerable learning, but men who likewise appeared to be men of love, acquainted by experience with true inward religion.

Some of these were burning and shining lights, persons famous in their generations, and such as had well deserved of the church of Christ, for standing in the gap against the overflowings of ungodliness.

It cannot be supposed that these holy and venerable men intended, at first, any more than to show that outward religion is worth nothing without the religion of the heart. God is a spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth. Therefore external worship is lost labor without a heart devoted to God.

The outward ordinances of God profit much when they advance inward holiness. But when they do not advance it, they are unprofitable and void. They are lighter than vanity. Yes, when they are used, as it were, in the place of this inward holiness, they are an utter abomination to the Lord.

title: When zeal outran caution
english: Yet it is not strange if some of these, strongly convinced of that horrid profanation of the ordinances of God which had spread itself over the whole church, and had very nearly driven true religion out of the world, spoke, in their fervent zeal for the glory of God and the recovery of souls from that fatal delusion, as if outward religion were absolutely nothing, as if it had no place in the religion of Christ.

It is not surprising at all if they did not always express themselves with sufficient caution. Unwary hearers might then believe that they condemned all outward means as altogether unprofitable, and as not designed by God to be the ordinary channels of conveying his grace into the souls of men.

No, it is not impossible that some of these holy men did at length fall into this opinion themselves. In particular, this may have been so with those who, not by choice but by the providence of God, were cut off from all these ordinances. Perhaps they were wandering up and down, having no certain abiding place, or dwelling in dens and caves of the earth.
These, experiencing the grace of God in themselves, though they were deprived of all outward means, might infer that the same grace would be given to those who deliberately abstained from them.

title: How easily the notion spreads
english: And experience shows how easily this notion spreads, and insinuates itself into the minds of men, especially of those who are thoroughly awakened out of the sleep of death, and begin to feel the weight of their sins, a burden too heavy to be borne.

These are usually impatient of their present state, and they try every way to escape from it. They are always ready to catch at any new thing, any new proposal of ease or happiness. They have probably tried most outward means, and found no ease in them. It may be they have found more and more of remorse, and fear, and sorrow, and condemnation.

It is easy, therefore, to persuade these that it is better for them to abstain from all those means. They are already weary of striving, as it seems, in vain, of laboring in the fire. They are therefore glad of any pretense to cast aside that in which their soul has no pleasure, to give over the painful strife, and to sink down into an indolent inactivity.

title: Whether there are any means of grace
english: In the following discourse, I propose to examine at large whether there are any means of grace.

title: What the means of grace are
english: By means of grace I understand outward signs, words, or actions, ordained by God, and appointed for this end, to be the ordinary channels by which he might convey to men preventing, justifying, or sanctifying grace.

I use this expression, means of grace, because I know none better, and because it has been generally used in the Christian church for many ages. In particular, it has been used by our own church, which directs us to bless God both for the means of grace and for the hopes of glory, and teaches us that a sacrament is an outward sign of inward grace, and a means by which we receive the same.

The chief of these means are prayer, whether in secret or with the great congregation; searching the scriptures, which implies reading, hearing, and meditating on them; and receiving the Lord's Supper, eating bread and drinking wine in remembrance of him. These we believe to be ordained by God as the ordinary channels of conveying his grace to the souls of men.

title: When the means miss their end
english: But we allow that the whole value of the means depends on their actually serving the end of religion. Consequently, all these means, when separate from the end, are less than nothing and vanity. If they do not actually lead to the knowledge and love of God, they are not acceptable in his sight. Rather, they are an abomination before him, a stink in his nostrils. He is weary of bearing them.

Above all, this is so if they are used as a kind of commutation, an exchange, for the religion they were designed to serve. It is not easy to find words for the enormous folly and wickedness of thus turning God's arms against himself, of keeping Christianity out of the heart by those very means which were ordained for the bringing of it in.

title: No power in the means themselves
english: We allow likewise that all outward means whatever, if separate from the Spirit of God, cannot profit at all. They cannot lead, in any degree, either to the knowledge or the love of God. Without controversy, the help that is done upon earth, he does it himself. It is he alone who, by his own almighty power, works in us what is pleasing in his sight. And all outward things, unless he works in them and by them, are mere weak and beggarly elements.

Whoever therefore imagines there is any intrinsic power in any means whatsoever greatly errs, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. We know that there is no inherent power in the words that are spoken in prayer, in the letter of scripture that is read, in the sound of it when it is heard, or in the bread and wine received in the Lord's Supper. It is God alone who is the giver of every good gift, the author of all grace. The whole power is of him, by which, through any of these, any blessing is conveyed to our soul.

We know likewise that he is able to give the same grace, though there were no means on the face of the earth. In this sense we may affirm that, with regard to God, there is no such thing as means, seeing he is equally able to work whatever pleases him, by any means, or by none at all.

title: They never atone for one sin
english: We allow further that the use of all means whatever will never atone for one sin. It is the blood of Christ alone by which any sinner can be reconciled to God. There is no other propitiation for our sins, no other fountain for sin and uncleanness.

Every believer in Christ is deeply convinced that there is no merit but in him, that there is no merit in any of his own works: not in uttering the prayer, or searching the scripture, or hearing the word of God, or eating of that bread and drinking of that cup.

So if no more is intended by the expression some have used, Christ is the only means of grace, than this, that he is the only meritorious cause of it, it cannot be gainsaid by any who know the grace of God.

title: Many still abuse the means
english: Yet once more. We allow, though it is a melancholy truth, that a large proportion of those who are called Christians do to this day abuse the means of grace, to the destruction of their souls. This is doubtless the case with all those who rest content in the form of godliness without the power.

Either they foolishly presume they are Christians already, because they do this and that, although Christ was never yet revealed in their hearts, nor the love of God shed abroad in them. Or else they suppose they shall certainly be so, merely because they use these means. They idly dream, though perhaps hardly conscious of it, either that there is some kind of power in the means, by which, sooner or later, they know not when, they shall certainly be made holy, or that there is a sort of merit in using them, which will surely move God to give them holiness, or to accept them without it.

title: By grace you are saved
english: So little do they understand that great foundation of the whole Christian building. By grace you are saved. You are saved from your sins, from the guilt and power of them. You are restored to the favor and image of God, not for any works, merits, or deservings of yours, but by the free grace, the mere mercy of God, through the merits of his well-beloved Son. You are thus saved, not by any power, wisdom, or strength which is in you, or in any other creature, but merely through the grace or power of the Holy Ghost, which works all in all.

title: How am I to wait
english: But the main question remains. We know this salvation is the gift and the work of God. But how, one may say who is convinced he does not have it, may I attain it?

If you say, Believe, and you shall be saved, he answers, True. But how shall I believe? You reply, Wait upon God. Well. But how am I to wait? In the means of grace, or outside them? Am I to wait for the grace of God which brings salvation by using these means, or by laying them aside?

title: He has not left us undetermined
english: It cannot possibly be conceived that the word of God should give no direction in so important a point, or that the Son of God, who came down from heaven for us men and for our salvation, should have left us undetermined with regard to a question in which our salvation is so nearly concerned.

And in fact, he has not left us undetermined. He has shown us the way in which we should go. We have only to consult the oracles of God, to inquire what is written there. And if we simply abide by their decision, there can remain no possible doubt.

title: Wait in the means he has ordained
english: According to this, according to the decision of holy writ, all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in the means which he has ordained, in using them, not in laying them aside.

title: Wait in the way of prayer
english: And first, all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in the way of prayer. This is the express direction of our Lord himself. In his sermon on the mount, after explaining at large what religion consists in, and describing the main branches of it, he adds, Ask, and it shall be given you. Seek, and you shall find. Knock, and it shall be opened to you. For everyone who asks receives, and he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it shall be opened. Matthew 7:7-8.

Here we are, in the plainest manner, directed to ask in order to receive, or as a means of receiving; to seek in order to find the grace of God, the pearl of great price; and to knock, to continue asking and seeking, if we would enter into his kingdom.

title: The Father gives to those who ask
english: That no doubt might remain, our Lord labors this point in a more particular manner. He appeals to every man's own heart. What man is there among you who, if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a serpent? If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall your Father who is in heaven, the Father of angels and men, the Father of the spirits of all flesh, give good things to those who ask him? Matthew 7:9-11.
Or, as he expresses himself on another occasion, including all good things in one, How much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him? Luke 11:13.

It should be particularly observed here that the persons directed to ask had not then received the Holy Spirit. Nevertheless our Lord directs them to use this means, and promises that it shall be effectual, that upon their asking they shall receive the Holy Spirit, from him whose mercy is over all his works.

title: The friend at midnight
english: The absolute necessity of using this means, if we would receive any gift from God, appears yet further from that remarkable passage which immediately precedes these words. And he said to them, whom he had just been teaching how to pray, Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go to him at midnight, and shall say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves? And he from within shall answer, Do not trouble me. I cannot rise and give you anything.

I say to you, Though he will not rise and give him anything, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needs. And I say to you, Ask, and it shall be given you. Luke 11:5, 7-9.

Though he will not give him anything, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needs. How could our blessed Lord more plainly declare that we may receive from God, by this means, by asking with importunity, what otherwise we should not receive at all?

title: The widow and the unjust judge
english: He also spoke another parable, to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint, until through this means they should receive from God whatever petition they asked of him.

There was in a city a judge who did not fear God, and did not regard man. And there was a widow in that city, and she came to him, saying, Avenge me of my adversary. And he would not for a while. But afterward he said within himself, Though I do not fear God, nor regard man, yet because this widow troubles me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me. Luke 18:1-4.

Our Lord himself has made the application of this. Hear what the unjust judge says. Because she continues to ask, because she will take no denial, therefore I will avenge her. And shall not God avenge his own elect, who cry day and night to him? I tell you, he will avenge them speedily, if they pray and do not faint.

title: Prayer in secret
english: A direction equally full and express, to wait for the blessings of God in private prayer, together with a positive promise that by this means we shall obtain the request of our lips, he has given us in those well-known words. Enter into your closet, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret shall reward you openly. Matthew 6:6.

title: If any of you lacks wisdom
english: If it is possible for any direction to be more clear, it is the one which God has given us by the apostle, with regard to prayer of every kind, public or private, and the blessing annexed to it.

If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all men liberally. If they ask. Otherwise, you have not, because you do not ask. James 4:2. And he does not upbraid, and it shall be given him. James 1:5.

If it is objected, But this is no direction to unbelievers, to those who do not know the pardoning grace of God, for the apostle adds, But let him ask in faith, otherwise let him not think that he shall receive anything from the Lord, I answer this. The meaning of the word faith, in this place, is fixed by the apostle himself, as if on purpose to answer this objection before it is made, in the words immediately following. Let him ask in faith, nothing wavering, nothing doubting. The Greek means not doubting at all. Not doubting that God hears his prayer, and will fulfill the desire of his heart.

The gross, blasphemous absurdity of supposing that faith, in this place, is taken in the full Christian meaning, appears from this. It supposes that the Holy Ghost directs a man who knows he does not have this faith, which is here called wisdom, to ask it of God, with a positive promise that it shall be given him, and then immediately adds that it shall not be given him unless he has it before he asks for it. But who can bear such a supposition? From this scripture, therefore, as well as from those cited above, we must infer that all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in the way of prayer.

title: Wait by searching the scriptures
english: Secondly, all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in searching the scriptures.

title: Search the scriptures
english: Our Lord's direction, with regard to the use of this means, is likewise plain and clear. Search the scriptures, he says to the unbelieving Jews, for they testify of me. John 5:39. And for this very end he directed them to search the scriptures, that they might believe in him.

The objection, that this is not a command, but only an assertion that they did search the scriptures, is shamelessly false. I desire those who urge it to let us know how a command can be more clearly expressed than in those terms. The Greek means, Search the scriptures. It is as peremptory as so many words can make it.

title: The Bereans
english: And what a blessing from God attends the use of this means appears from what is recorded concerning the Bereans. After hearing Saint Paul, they searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. Therefore many of them believed. They found the grace of God in the way which he had ordained. Acts 17:11-12.

It is probable, indeed, that in some of those who had received the word with all readiness of mind, faith came, as the same apostle speaks, by hearing, and was only confirmed by reading the scriptures. But it was observed above that, under the general term of searching the scriptures, both hearing, reading, and meditating are contained.

title: Wise to salvation
english: And that this is a means by which God not only gives, but also confirms and increases, true wisdom, we learn from the words of Saint Paul to Timothy. From a child you have known the holy scriptures, which are able to make you wise to salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 3:15.

The same truth, namely, that this is the great means God has ordained for conveying his manifold grace to man, is delivered in the fullest manner that can be conceived, in the words which immediately follow. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and consequently all scripture is infallibly true, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, to the end that the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished to all good works. 2 Timothy 3:16-17.

title: Do not make light of the Old Testament
english: It should be observed that this is spoken primarily and directly of the scriptures which Timothy had known from a child. Those must have been the scriptures of the Old Testament, for the New Testament was not then written.

How far, then, was Saint Paul from making light of the Old Testament? He was not a whit behind the very chief of the apostles, nor therefore, I presume, behind any man now upon the earth. Behold this, lest you one day wonder and perish, you who make so small account of one half of the oracles of God.

Yes, and that half of which the Holy Ghost expressly declares that it is profitable, as a means ordained by God, for this very thing, for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, to the end that the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished to all good works.

title: A light in a dark place
english: Nor is this profitable only for the men of God, for those who already walk in the light of his countenance, but also for those who are yet in darkness, seeking him whom they do not know.

Thus Saint Peter says, We have also a more sure word of prophecy. Literally, and we have the prophetic word more sure. It is confirmed by our being eye-witnesses of his majesty, and by hearing the voice which came from the excellent glory. To that prophetic word, for so he calls the holy scriptures, you do well to take heed, as to a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns, and the day-star arises in your hearts. 2 Peter 1:19.
Let all, therefore, who desire that day to dawn upon their hearts, wait for it in searching the scriptures.

title: The Lord's Supper
english: Thirdly, all who desire an increase of the grace of God are to wait for it in partaking of the Lord's Supper. For this also is a direction he himself has given.

The same night in which he was betrayed, he took bread, and broke it, and said, Take, eat. This is my body, that is, the sacred sign of my body. Do this in remembrance of me. Likewise he took the cup, saying, This cup is the new testament, or covenant, in my blood, the sacred sign of that covenant. Do this in remembrance of me. For as often as you eat this bread, and drink this cup, you show forth the Lord's death till he comes. 1 Corinthians 11:23.
You openly exhibit the same, by these visible signs, before God, and angels, and men. You manifest your solemn remembrance of his death, until he comes in the clouds of heaven.

Only let a man first examine himself, whether he understands the nature and design of this holy institution, and whether he really desires to be himself made conformable to the death of Christ. And so, nothing doubting, let him eat of that bread, and drink of that cup. 1 Corinthians 11:28.

Here, then, the direction first given by our Lord is expressly repeated by the apostle. Let him eat. Let him drink. Both are in the imperative mood. These words do not imply a bare permission only, but a clear, explicit command. It is a command to all those who either already are filled with peace and joy in believing, or can truly say, The remembrance of our sins is grievous to us, the burden of them is intolerable.

title: The communion of his body and blood
english: And that this is also an ordinary, stated means of receiving the grace of God is evident from those words of the apostle which occur in the preceding chapter. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion, or communication, of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? 1 Corinthians 10:16.

Is not the eating of that bread, and the drinking of that cup, the outward, visible means by which God conveys into our souls all that spiritual grace, that righteousness, and peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost, which were purchased by the body of Christ once broken, and the blood of Christ once shed for us? Let all, therefore, who truly desire the grace of God, eat of that bread and drink of that cup.

title: Objections against the way
english: But as plainly as God has pointed out the way in which he will be inquired after, innumerable are the objections which men, wise in their own eyes, have from time to time raised against it. It may be needful to consider a few of these, not because they are of weight in themselves, but because they have so often been used, especially of late years, to turn the lame out of the way. Yes, to trouble and subvert those who did run well, while Satan appeared as an angel of light.

title: You cannot use them without trusting
english: The first and chief of these is, You cannot use these means, as you call them, without trusting in them. I ask, where is this written? I expect you to show me plain scripture for your assertion. Otherwise I dare not receive it, because I am not convinced that you are wiser than God.

If it really had been as you assert, it is certain Christ must have known it. And if he had known it, he would surely have warned us. He would have revealed it long ago. Therefore, because he has not, because there is not one tittle of this in the whole revelation of Jesus Christ, I am as fully assured that your assertion is false as that this revelation is of God.

However, leave them off for a short time, to see whether you trusted in them or not. So I am to disobey God, in order to know whether I trust in obeying him? And do you avow this advice? Do you deliberately teach men to do evil, that good may come? O tremble at the sentence of God against such teachers. Their damnation is just.

No, if you are troubled when you leave them off, it is plain you trusted in them. By no means. If I am troubled when I willfully disobey God, it is plain his Spirit is still striving with me. But if I am not troubled at willful sin, it is plain I am given up to a reprobate mind.

But what do you mean by trusting in them? Looking for the blessing of God in them? Believing that if I wait in this way, I shall attain what otherwise I should not? So I do. And so I will, God being my helper, even to my life's end. By the grace of God I will thus trust in them till the day of my death. That is, I will believe that whatever God has promised, he is faithful also to perform. And seeing he has promised to bless me in this way, I trust it shall be according to his word.

title: Seeking salvation by works
english: It has been objected, secondly, This is seeking salvation by works. Do you know the meaning of the expression you use? What is seeking salvation by works? In the writings of Saint Paul, it means either seeking to be saved by observing the ritual works of the Mosaic law, or expecting salvation for the sake of our own works, by the merit of our own righteousness.
But how is either of these implied in my waiting in the way God has ordained, and expecting that he will meet me there, because he has promised to do so?

I do expect that he will fulfill his word, that he will meet and bless me in this way. Yet not for the sake of any works which I have done, nor for the merit of my righteousness, but merely through the merits, and sufferings, and love of his Son, in whom he is always well pleased.

title: Christ is the only means of grace
english: It has been vehemently objected, thirdly, that Christ is the only means of grace. I answer, this is mere playing upon words. Explain your term, and the objection vanishes away.

When we say, Prayer is a means of grace, we understand a channel through which the grace of God is conveyed. When you say, Christ is the means of grace, you understand the sole price and purchaser of it, or that no man comes to the Father but through him. And who denies it? But this is utterly wide of the question.

title: In the way of his ordinances
english: But does not the scripture, it has been objected, fourthly, direct us to wait for salvation? Does not David say, My soul waits upon God, for from him comes my salvation? And does not Isaiah teach us the same thing, saying, O Lord, we have waited for you?

All this cannot be denied. Since salvation is the gift of God, we are undoubtedly to wait on him for it. But how shall we wait? If God himself has appointed a way, can you find a better way of waiting for him? But that he has appointed a way has been shown at large, and also what that way is. The very words of the prophet which you cite put this out of all question. For the whole sentence runs thus: In the way of your judgments, or ordinances, O Lord, we have waited for you. Isaiah 26:8.

And in the very same way David waited, as his own words abundantly testify. I have waited for your saving health, O Lord, and have kept your law. Teach me, O Lord, the way of your statutes, and I shall keep it to the end.

title: Stand still and see
english: Yes, say some, but God has appointed another way. Stand still, and see the salvation of God.
Let us examine the scriptures to which you refer. The first of them, with the context, runs thus.

And when Pharaoh drew near, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and they were sorely afraid. And they said to Moses, Because there were no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in the wilderness? And Moses said to the people, Do not fear. Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord. And the Lord said to Moses, Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward. But lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it. And the children of Israel shall go on dry ground through the midst of the sea. Exodus 14:10.
This was the salvation of God which they stood still to see, by marching forward with all their might.

The other passage in which this expression occurs stands thus. There came some who told Jehoshaphat, saying, There comes a great multitude against you, from beyond the sea. And Jehoshaphat feared, and set himself to seek the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah. And Judah gathered themselves together to ask help of the Lord. Out of all the cities they came to seek the Lord. And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation, in the house of the Lord. Then upon Jahaziel came the Spirit of the Lord. And he said, Do not be dismayed by reason of this great multitude. Tomorrow go down against them. You shall not need to fight in this battle. Set yourselves. Stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord. And they arose early in the morning and went forth. And when they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushes against the children of Moab, Ammon, and Mount Seir, and everyone helped to destroy another. 2 Chronicles 20:2.
Such was the salvation which the children of Judah saw. But how does all this prove that we ought not to wait for the grace of God in the means which he has ordained?

title: Not the ordinances of Christ
english: I shall mention but one objection more, which indeed does not properly belong to this head. Nevertheless, because it has been so frequently urged, I may not wholly pass it by.
Does not Saint Paul say, If you are dead with Christ, why are you subject to ordinances? Colossians 2:20. Therefore a Christian, one who is dead with Christ, need not use the ordinances any more.

So you say, If I am a Christian, I am not subject to the ordinances of Christ. Surely, by the absurdity of this, you must see at the first glance that the ordinances mentioned here cannot be the ordinances of Christ. They must be the Jewish ordinances, to which it is certain a Christian is no longer subject.
And the same undeniably appears from the words immediately following. Do not touch, do not taste, do not handle. All of these evidently refer to the ancient ordinances of the Jewish law.
So this objection is the weakest of all. And in spite of all, that great truth must stand unshaken, that all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in the means which he has ordained.

title: The order and the manner
english: But this being allowed, that all who desire the grace of God are to wait for it in the means he has ordained, it may still be inquired how those means should be used, both as to the order and the manner of using them.

title: How God generally leads a sinner
english: With regard to the order, we may observe that there is a kind of order in which God himself is generally pleased to use these means in bringing a sinner to salvation. A stupid, senseless wretch is going on in his own way, not having God in all his thoughts, when God comes upon him unawares. Perhaps it is by an awakening sermon or conversation, perhaps by some awful providence, or it may be by an immediate stroke of his convincing Spirit, without any outward means at all.

Having now a desire to flee from the wrath to come, he purposely goes to hear how it may be done. If he finds a preacher who speaks to the heart, he is amazed, and begins searching the scriptures, whether these things are so. The more he hears and reads, the more convinced he is, and the more he meditates on them, day and night.

Perhaps he finds some other book which explains and enforces what he has heard and read in scripture. And by all these means, the arrows of conviction sink deeper into his soul. He begins also to talk of the things of God, which are ever uppermost in his thoughts, yes, and to talk with God, to pray to him, although through fear and shame he scarcely knows what to say.

But whether he can speak or not, he cannot but pray, even if only in groans which cannot be uttered. Yet, being in doubt whether the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity will regard such a sinner as him, he wants to pray with those who know God, with the faithful, in the great congregation.

But here he observes others go up to the table of the Lord. He considers, Christ has said, Do this. How is it that I do not? I am too great a sinner. I am not fit. I am not worthy. After struggling with these scruples a while, he breaks through. And thus he continues in God's way, in hearing, reading, meditating, praying, and partaking of the Lord's Supper, until God, in the manner that pleases him, speaks to his heart, Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.

title: What to recommend to each soul
english: By observing this order of God, we may learn what means to recommend to any particular soul. If any of these will reach a stupid, careless sinner, it is probably hearing or conversation. To such a person, therefore, we might recommend these, if he ever has any thought about salvation.

To one who begins to feel the weight of his sins, not only hearing the word of God, but reading it too, and perhaps other serious books, may be a means of deeper conviction. May you not advise him also to meditate on what he reads, that it may have its full force upon his heart? Yes, and to speak of it, and not be ashamed, particularly among those who walk in the same path.

When trouble and heaviness take hold upon him, should you not then earnestly exhort him to pour out his soul before God? Always to pray, and not to faint? And when he feels the worthlessness of his own prayers, are you not to work together with God, and remind him of going up into the house of the Lord, and praying with all who fear him?

But if he does this, the dying word of his Lord will soon be brought to his remembrance. That is a plain intimation that this is the time when we should second the motions of the blessed Spirit. And thus we may lead him, step by step, through all the means which God has ordained, not according to our own will, but just as the providence and the Spirit of God go before and open the way.

title: A thousand different ways
english: Yet, as we find no command in holy writ for any particular order to be observed in this, so neither do the providence and the Spirit of God adhere to any order without variation. The means into which different men are led, and in which they find the blessing of God, are varied, transposed, and combined together, in 1,000 different ways.

Yet still our wisdom is to follow the leadings of his providence and his Spirit. We are to be guided in this, more especially as to the means in which we ourselves seek the grace of God, partly by his outward providence, giving us the opportunity of using sometimes one means, sometimes another, and partly by our experience of that by which his free Spirit is pleased most to work in our heart.

And in the meantime, the sure and general rule for all who groan for the salvation of God is this. Whenever opportunity serves, use all the means which God has ordained. For who knows in which God will meet you, with the grace that brings salvation?

title: God is above all means
english: As to the manner of using them, on which indeed it wholly depends whether they should convey any grace at all to the one who uses them, it behooves us, first, always to retain a lively sense that God is above all means. Take care, therefore, not to limit the Almighty. He does whatever he pleases, and whenever it pleases him.

He can convey his grace, either in or out of any of the means which he has appointed. Perhaps he will. Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor? Look, then, every moment for his appearing. Let it be at the hour you are employed in his ordinances, or before, or after that hour, or when you are hindered from them. He is not hindered. He is always ready, always able, always willing to save. It is the Lord. Let him do what seems good to him.

title: There is no power in the work itself
english: Secondly, before you use any means, let it be deeply impressed upon your soul. There is no power in this. It is in itself a poor, dead, empty thing. Separate from God, it is a dry leaf, a shadow. Neither is there any merit in my using this, nothing intrinsically pleasing to God, nothing by which I deserve any favor at his hands, no, not a drop of water to cool my tongue. But because God bids, therefore I do. Because he directs me to wait in this way, therefore here I wait for his free mercy, from which comes my salvation.

Settle this in your heart, that the old Latin phrase opus operatum, the mere work done, profits nothing. There is no power to save but in the Spirit of God, no merit but in the blood of Christ. Consequently, even what God ordains conveys no grace to the soul, if you do not trust in him alone. On the other hand, he who does truly trust in him cannot fall short of the grace of God, even though he were cut off from every outward ordinance, even though he were shut up in the center of the earth.

title: Seek God alone
english: Thirdly, in using all means, seek God alone. In and through every outward thing, look only to the power of his Spirit, and the merits of his Son. Beware that you do not stick in the work itself. If you do, it is all lost labor. Nothing short of God can satisfy your soul. Therefore fix your eye on him, in all, through all, and above all.

title: Use them as means
english: Remember also to use all means as means, as ordained, not for their own sake, but in order to the renewal of your soul in righteousness and true holiness. If, therefore, they actually tend to this, well. But if not, they are dung and dross.

title: Do not congratulate yourself
english: Lastly, after you have used any of these, take care how you value yourself upon it, how you congratulate yourself, as having done some great thing. This is turning all into poison. Think, If God was not there, what does this avail? Have I not been adding sin to sin? How long, O Lord? Save, or I perish. O do not lay this sin to my charge.

If God was there, if his love flowed into your heart, you have forgotten, as it were, the outward work. You see, you know, you feel, God is all in all. Be abased. Sink down before him. Give him all the praise. Let God in all things be glorified through Christ Jesus. Let all your bones cry out, My song shall always be of the loving-kindness of the Lord. With my mouth I will ever be telling of your truth, from one generation to another.
